full_judgment: 9. On a perusal of the record it appears that the present pre-emptor-opposite parties filed the pre-emption case on the averment that they are the co-sharer tenants in the case holding and their co- sharer pre-emptee (seller) opposite party No.3 Md Rafiqullah sold 24 decimals of land appertaining to khatian No. 157 to the vendee opposite party Nos. 1-2 by a registered kabala No. 11986 dated 21-12-1997 beyond their knowledge and the vendee-pre-emptee Nos. 1-2 are strangers to the case land. In order to prove the case the pre-emptor-opposite parties examined 2 witnesses including pre-emptor opposite party No.1, while pre-emptee-petitioner examined only 1 (one) witness namely, Abdul Malek and both the parties exhibited documents in support of their respective claim. On going through the evidence of PW 1, PW 2 and OPW 1 and the concurrent findings of the Courts below, it appears that the application for pre-emption is not defective for non-joinder of necessary parties inasmuch as the learned Advocate for the pre-emptee-opposite parties by filing an application informed the Court that the case does not suffer from defect of party. Thus, it appears to me that the pre-emption case cannot fail on account of non-joinder of necessary parties and therefore, the case of Abdul Wahab vs Samad Ali reported in 33 DLR (AD) 113 referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in this context for non-impleading of necessary parties is of no assistance to the present pre-emptee- petitioner. Next comes the 2nd branch of argument as advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner (pre-emptee-opposite party) that the deed under pre-emption was, in fact, a deed of mortgage but due to mistake the kabala was written as a sale deed instead of mortgage deed. But, on going through the evidence and concurrent findings of the Courts below it appears to me that the instant pre-emption case was filed on 24-3-1998 and Title Suit No. 30 of 1998 was instituted on 22-3-1998 i.e. two days back from the filing of the pre-emption case, and the suit was decreed on 30-4-1998 in terms of solenama dated 2-4-1998. Therefore, it is evident that the solenama was filed within 18 days from the institution of the said suit in order to obtain a decree declaring the deed in question is a mortgage deed and whereupon, both the Courts below correctly on considering the material evidence on record and the other attending circumstances, concurrently held that the decree was obtained in Title Suit No. 30 of 98 in terms of solenama between purchaser (pre- emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-2) and seller (pre-emptee-opposite party No.3) declaring sale deed dated 21-12-1997 is a mortgage deed which, in fact, is a fraudulent soleh decree and such colourable transaction having been made to defend the right of the pre-emption available to the pre-ernptors. The alleged transfer of the disputed land in between the vendor opposite party No.3 and vendee-opposite party Nos. 1-2 is an out and out sale. Thus, the grievances of the learned Advocate for the petitioner are found to be without any foundation.
